newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures alike, were expected to open steady to 0.250 cent per lb higher, livestock analysts said.
Firmer-than-expected cash markets were expected to encourage early support in live cattle futures and prices were seen ranging steady to higher.
Fair weekend beef movement was cited as supporting boxed beef prices and packers showed good interest for fed cattle Monday, analysts said.
Spillover demand from pork pits is also expected as beef will likely benefit from less-than-expected pork supplies the remainder of the year, they said.

Feeder cattle futures were seen posting gains following Monday's advance to new contract highs and highest price since August 1994. The sharp gain in the latest CME feeder cattle index and lower corn futures indications were expected to spark further demand.
The latest CME feeder cattle index up up $1.22 to $80.30 per cwt, the highest level since April 21, 1994.
Feeder cattle supplies remain tight and are expected to continue this way into the fall, analysts said.
